stories-66-10-unfaithful-wives-of-noah-a.title: The Wives of Noah and Lot Betraying Their Righteous Husbands
stories-66-10-unfaithful-wives-of-noah-a.note: Surah 66:10 presents the wives of Noah and Lot as disbelievers who betrayed their righteous husbands, matching Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 where Lot's wife betrays the angelic guests to the Sodomites by asking neighbors for salt.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that the betrayal in 66:10 was in religion rather than marital chastity: Noah's wife called her husband mad and informed on believers, while Lot's wife signaled the presence of handsome guests to the people of Sodom.
discussion.reply: Genesis 19:26 states that Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt without mentioning any plot against the guests. Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 supplies the narrative of betrayal, recording that she went to her neighbors asking for salt so the townsmen of Sodom would learn that guests were staying in Lot's house.

stories-66-10-unfaithful-wives-of-noah-a.quranEn: God has struck a parable for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them. Neither of them was of any use at all to either of them against God, when it was said, ‘Enter the Fire, both of you, with the ones who enter!’
quranHighlights: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot
They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them.

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 (Lot's Wife Betraying the Guests by Asking Neighbors for Salt)
sources.en: “His wife looked behind him, [and she became a pillar of salt]” – Rabbi Yitzḥak said: This was because she sinned with salt on that night that the angels came to Lot. What did she do? She went to all her neighbors and said to them: ‘Give me salt, as we have guests,’ and her intention was that the residents of the city should become aware of them. That is why “she became a pillar of salt.”
highlights: sinned with salt on that night that the angels came to Lot
‘Give me salt, as we have guests,’ and her intention was that the residents of the city should become aware of them.

stories-66-12-mary-daughter-of-imran-spi.title: Mary Styled 'Daughter of 'Imran' (Amram of Numbers 26:59)
stories-66-12-mary-daughter-of-imran-spi.note: Surah 66:12 directly calls Mary, the mother of Jesus, 'Mary, daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana), assigning to her the patronymic of Miriam, daughter of Amram and sister of Aaron and Moses in Numbers 26:59.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 66:12 names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' either after her biological father from the Davidic or priestly line, or by ancestral lineage to the Mosaic 'Imran (Amram), while Gabriel breathed into the sleeve of her garment.
discussion.reply: Whereas 19:28 addresses Mary as 'sister of Aaron' and 3:35 speaks of the 'wife of 'Imran,' 66:12 explicitly names Mary 'daughter of 'Imran' (Maryama bnata 'Imrana). In the Hebrew Bible and Septuagint (Numbers 26:59; Exodus 6:20), Amram ('Imran) is the Levitical father of Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam (Greek Mariam), thirteen centuries before Jesus' mother Mary (whose father in early Christian tradition is Joachim).
